reviews.comment: I loved this class! It was done over zoom. You'll have a paper every week and two readings to read beforehand. She really cares more about you actually learning and participating in writing and class discussion more than grading difficult. Loved this and would 100% recommend!

GREAT. Although there were many papers to write over the semester it really helps doing the final paper at the end of the semester. Able to combine past ideas, articles, etc. into final paper. Basically writing final paper throughout the semester. This was an online class so not really sure what in person would have looked like. but overall great
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Respected

reviews.comment: This professor calls herself an "award-winning Team Rhetoric professor," but her reputation comes mostly from Twitter rants about Trump, not real expertise in communication. With shallow insights and minimal rigor, she's no authority and will likely fade into obscurity. Friendly and lax on attendance, but lacking depth. Look elsewhere for quality!

Professor Mercieca is very knowledgeable politically, HOWEVER, I recommend that you look up her writings/twitter before taking her class. There is obvious bias within her class and she can get defensive if you challenge a fact she gives. But overall she is very fair and a good professor, I will be taking another one of her classes.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Mercieca was very very sweet, classes weren't mandatory but I always felt bad missing bc no one would go. She also gives extra credit for attendance sometimes. We had a two-page essay every week, a project, and a final paper, but the class material was very interesting.

This was a discussion-heavy and paper-heavy class. Two-page paper almost every week, and the final was a 6-8 page paper that built on a previous one written. She graded very leniently, and I enjoyed listening to what she had to say. Attendance was somewhat mandatory with a password-locked one-question quiz to ensure you're in class.

Ironically, you get fed a lot of propaganda in this class. Says she is "unbiased" but has openly admitted to thinking free will doesn't exist and that religion is "mental violence." Is nice, knowledgable, and gives a lot of 100s, but be prepared to hear from only one perspective- even left-leaning people in the class think she's very extreme.

She is a very nice lady and is very knowledgeable about several topics. I liked her but she doesnt receive an amazing response from our class so she is not very engaging. Class is interesting, most learning is up to you to read the readings for the day. Main thing I dont like is she pushes liberal agenda on the class but reiterates shes not biased.

This is my last year in college and I can honestly say this has been one of the most informative classes. Dr. Mercieca is one of my favorite professors I've had. Definitely take this class and participate because you will definitely get something very valuable out of it. She wants her students to succeed and is incredibly helpful!

All around sweet and funny lady. She really values your understanding of the material and your improvement over trying to grade really hard. She allowed us to correct and resubmit all our papers and was so helpful if you went in to ask her specific questions. She is very interactive and a very intelligent woman who has published a lot of works
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Mercieca is an amazing human being and treats her students like real human beings. I was honored to take her for my writing intensive course (propaganda). She loves what she does and it shows in the classroom. TAKE HER. She is the best.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: I took Professor Mercieca's course during study abroad in Italy, so the course was probably different than it would be in Cstat. Still, I HIGHLY recommend taking her class. She is sweet, funny, and she genuinely wants to help you make an A. I wrote a lot of papers, but it was never an overwhelming amount. I definitely would take her course again!

This was the only writing intensive left so I took it reluctantly but I'm glad I did. I ended up with a 100 as my final grade! We had 4-5 papers total, but each can be resubmitted as many times as you want, 4-5 debates (just for fun, not graded), and a take home final. Attendance is not mandatory but you should go because it is a lot of information
I got a B in this course, and it's very straightforward. You attend the course, write the notes, and read the material, not hard to get an A.

Good instructor overall. She is obviously liberal, it comes out in her class discussions and readings. However, she is open to debate and does not grade people lower for not agreeing with her views. I did note that she would sometimes make claims that simply were not true, such as 10% of Americans are in prison. Not a bad class overall.
Communist. One of those out to "cure" Texas A&M and our backwards ways.

I love this Professor! She is such a joy. So bubbly and nice! Though, I will say, if you take her class be prepared to come to class everyday. Though attendance isn't mandatory, her notes and lecture are intensive. Bring a laptop if you can and be prepared to write ALOT of notes. Ive only taken her midterm, but I made a B. Would take her again. :)

I feel bad giving her a mediocre grade on difficulty, because although her "difficulty" score is a little low, I'm fairly certain the people grading her this way are the same unconcerned students incessantly chatting it up around me during her lecture, making it difficult to even hear--much less focus on--what she's saying. She's very friendly and between her and the TA's, they welcome questions, so it's not hard to get things clarified that you don't understand. You'd have to really not be taking the class seriously enough to get anything lower than a B, and an A is very do-able.
